name: Creating a Dictionary of Student-Scores Pairs (Case 1)
description: Assume we have a list of students and a list of their corresponding test scores. Construct a program that has a function which receives these two lists and returns a dictionary that maps each student to the scores of that student.\nFor example, if the student list is ['Sam', 'Kim', 'Sam'] and the scores list is [15, 10, 14], the program creates the following dictionary:\n{'Sam': [15, 14], 'Kim': [10]}

commentList:
We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function create_dictionary that takes a list of students (referred by variable std_lst) and a list of their corresponding test scores (referred by variable test_lst) and returns a dictionary that maps each student to the scores of that student.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented.

We first need to define a dictionary referred by variable res_dict for storing the scores of each student. We initialize it with an empty dictionary by setting it to a pair of braces {}.

We need this dictionary to store key-value pairs where each key represents a student and the value that is mapped to that key represents the list of the student's scores.

5.content: #Step 1.2: Update the dictionary entries as we iterate through the indexes in the given lists

commentList:
We need to get each student and corresponding test scores for that student. We can do this by iterating over the indexes in the given lists.

We need the list indexes to start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including the list length. We get this sequence by calling the range(len(std_lst)) function.
Note that the function len(std_lst) returns the number of the values in the students list. Also note that we could use len(test_lst) in the range function as both lists have equal number of values.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

To determine if the student at index i of the students list already exists as the key in the dictionary, we employ the in operator to test membership. Because the in operator implicitly scans the keys in the dictionary looking for a match.
std_lst[i] gives us the student at index i in the students list.
If the student at index i of the students list already exists as the key in the dictionary, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

When the student at index i of the students list already exists as the key in the dictionary, we call the function append(test_lst[i]) to add the test score at index i of the score list to the end of the list that holds student's test scores.
When the student at index i of the students list does not exist as the key in the dictionary, we need to add a new entry to the dictionary for the student.

The statement inside the body of this else statement is executed when the student at index i of the students list does not exist as the key in the dictionary. Otherwise, the body of this else statement is skipped.

We need to add the student at index i in the students list as a new key to the dictionary. We need to initialize the value mapped to this key with a list that has the test score at index i of the scores list.
Now that we created the dictionary, we need to return it.
The return statement, when reached, ends the function call and sends the result back to the caller.
We define list referred by variable names to hold the students names. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].
We define list referred by variable scores to hold the test scores. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the content of the dictionary returned from the function call.
Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned dictionary from the function call in a variable. We could use the dictionary returned from the function call directly in the print function.
Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared. Also note that we can see the content of the dictionary by calling the print function and passing the dictionary to that.
